items.title: Learning curves - loss vs training-set size, extrapolated
items.note: LANDED 2026-09-08. Gate 1 passed for ALL FIVE families -- the row arm's 100% point is the published refit and reproduced the v11 headline bit-identically (abs delta 0.000e+00 on p10/p50/p90/cliff/stint life). HEADLINE 1: no family is still gaining from ROWS at 100% -- every family's 75->100% leg is inside its floor. The degradation trio did gain over the full 4x range (1.9-4.5x floor) and is exhausted by 75%; the cliff classifier gained NOTHING across the whole range (0.05x floor). HEADLINE 2: the extrapolated intercept does not bind for any family -- p90 and cliff pin b at the upper bound 3.0 (a restatement of the plateau, not an extrapolation), stint life pins b at the lower bound 0.02 leaving c unidentifiable (LOO range 0.9722-1.7783 against a claimed headroom of 0.2865), and p10/p50 have leave-one-fraction-out spreads 3.0x and 3.3x the headroom they claim. The learning-curve instrument returns the same verdict ceiling.py already returns: it does not bind. That strengthens 01b rather than weakening it. HEADLINE 3, from a THIRD ARM added mid-item and logged in the leaf doc: the two specified arms cannot separate regime coverage from recency, so the season ladder was rerun from the newest end and read at matched n. Recency wins -- for p50, cliff and stint life the newer window beats the older at EVERY matched n (stint life by 14-57x its floor). The one unambiguous result: the CLIFF CLASSIFIER IS BETTER TRAINED ON 2021-2023 THAN ON 2018-2023, 0.39318 vs 0.38027 macro-F1, +0.01291 = 3.71x its own reseed floor, by deleting 46% of its training rows. NOT ACTED ON -- filed as 05d. Mechanism verified: HYPERSOFT/SUPERSOFT/ULTRASOFT are three of the eight ordinal `compound` levels, occur only in 2018 (8,777 rows, over half that season) and in no 2024 eval row. METHOD CORRECTION carried in the leaf doc: the reseed floor alone is the WRONG denominator for a last-leg gain, because the 75% point carries subsample variance the reseed floor never measures; under the correct composite 2*sqrt(sd_75^2/3 + sd_reseed^2) stint life's last leg is inside noise, where the reseed floor alone reads it as a real gain. Reseed floors computed for p10 and p90 for the first time: p10 0.00805, p50 0.01332, p90 0.00773, cliff 0.00349, stint life 0.00281. Probe throwaway, scratchpad only; nothing committed, no model or warehouse touched.

items.title: Empirical noise floor - difference-based, stratified, bracketed
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-09. Built as the difference-based / matched-cell estimator R1 specified, pre-registered in full, and it fails its own falsification gate at the headline level on 2 of 3 heads. Two method findings survive it. (1) DEFECT 1'S PROPOSED FIX WAS NOT IDENTIFIED: d = y1 - y2 is exactly symmetric for every eps, so fitting a skew-capable family to d returns zero skew by construction -- the leaf doc has been corrected. The construction defect 1 rejects (centre-and-pool) is the one that works, with Sum(c^2)=1-1/m, Sum(c^3)=0 at m=2 and 2/9 at m=3, Sum(c^4)>0 always: tail weight is identified from pairs, skew needs m>=3. (2) THE SYNTHETIC ARM CAUGHT TWO REAL RULE DEFECTS before any floor was quoted -- a row-selection rule that selected on the coordinate the noise is heteroscedastic in (-40% at L0/L1), and a shape standardisation on strata so fine it destroyed the tails it existed to preserve (-37% on excess kurtosis; the unstandardised pooled version was +68% the other way). Three instruments now agree that the trio's remaining headroom is smaller than anything the programme can resolve.
items.closed: CLOSED 2026-09-09 as a completed measurement, not as a failure. Every clause of the definition of done was delivered: the synthetic recovery passed at the claimed shape (sigma^2 -1.98% +/- 2.14%, end-to-end p50 floor +3.4%), the admissible-neighbour distance was measured (median 4.275 vs 6.829 for random pairs, ratio 0.626, distribution nowhere near zero), the floor was published as a bracket with the metric, NaN treatment and weighting rule stated, the falsification gate was checked at all 18 ladder x quantile points and every violation reported as an instrument failure, and the result was reconciled against 01a. THE ANSWER IS THAT THE INSTRUMENT DOES NOT BIND on p10 or p50: at the three-coordinate headline level the floor comes back ABOVE the loss it is meant to bound (0.5654 vs 0.5188; 1.0641 vs 1.0163). The mechanism is measured, not guessed -- the conditioning ladder is still falling at L3 (-10.4% to L4, a further -13.3% to L5), so the residual mean-function bias at three matched coordinates is larger than the headroom being resolved. R1's dimension constraint therefore binds harder than it was stated to: it is not only that 33-D is outside the regime, it is that the <=3-D fallback lacks the resolution to answer the question either. p90 is the only head where floor and achieved separate (0.4914 vs 0.5600, +12.3%), and the separation is about the size of its own error bar once the 4.5% race component is added back -- handed to 11a as directional, not established. DO NOT RE-OPEN without one of: (a) an eval population with repeated circuits inside a season, which would restore the different-race constraint this one had to drop because every 2024 circuit hosts exactly one race; (b) 08d's C1-C5 identity, which would make a cross-season same-circuit match well defined; or (c) a lower-dimensional target. A better fitter is not new evidence -- unit.py shows the arithmetic recovers to +/-0.5%.

items.title: Tier 2 leakage ruling - the 5-lap field-median bucket (NOT the centred/backward binary)
items.note: RULED 2026-09-08. Barred as constructed. The item's binary (centred vs backward) fits neither: FLOOR(lap/5)*5 is a fixed BLOCK bucket. Measured over all 2,206,939 rows by reconstructing corners_with_keys - mean forward reach 1.877 laps (R5 estimated 'about two'), 77.83% of lap-groups reach forward, 38.45% of the average median's rows are drawn from laps that had not yet run; by block position 0/1/2/3/4 the forward share is 76.00/56.44/40.00/20.67/0.00%. What decides it: DEGRADATION_TARGET is next_5_lap_cumulative_jump_s (t+1..t+5) and max forward reach is 4 laps, so every contaminating lap sits INSIDE the label's own window - and at block position 0, 95.55% of rows are scored against a baseline holding a mean 3.351 of that driver's OWN future laps. Not point-in-time correct. Materiality measured too, and reported as suggestive not decisive: isolating delta = block - trailing, corr(delta,label) = +0.0344 [+0.0047,+0.0667] at positions 0-3 vs +0.0083 [-0.0143,+0.0324] at the zero-reach position-4 control, paired race-clustered difference +0.0261 [-0.0008,+0.0531], one-sided p=0.027; the control is imperfectly matched, so the ruling rests on the deterministic construction, not on this. The rebuild costs no signal - trailing's marginal |corr| with the label is equal or higher at every block position - and costs 2.22pp of lap-grain coverage, essentially all of it lap 2, which has no predecessor. Bar is scoped to ML admission: mart_corner_skill_driver consumes the same columns descriptively with no forward label and is NOT barred. Confirms 08b's premise - the reach lives entirely in a GROUP BY scope, so audit_forward_window read this model as clean the whole time. Fix is 02g; 02c now depends on 02g, not on 02a.

items.title: Rebuild the corner field median as a trailing window
items.landed: Built 2026-09-11. Replaced FLOOR(lap/5)*5 block buckets in int_corner_skill_residuals with RANGE BETWEEN 5 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING trailing window (trailing-5, not expanding: keeps width comparable to block, avoids pooling early/late track states per 02d's pattern). RANGE preserves field median semantics (all drivers at each lap level); 1 PRECEDING enforces backward-only construction. field_corner_sample_n is NULL (not 0) when count < 5 to propagate NULLs to residuals consistently. Lap 2 correctly returns NULL for all corners (deterministic, non-leaking coverage loss of 21.4pp on laps ≤ 6, concentrated on lap 2 which has no predecessor - no expanding window rescue attempted since lap 1 reaches zero laps regardless). Test assert_corner_trailing_window_no_forward_reach passes (lap 2 NULL gate). Trailing-median/trailing-observation-count macros (already existing from 08e rebuild) are now called here; 02d will reuse. Definition of done satisfied: backward-only median in place, test verifies no row baseline draws on lap t or future, lap-2 NULL rule documented in schema.yml with coverage figures, mart_corner_skill_driver rebuilt (outputs changed as expected), model_hashes.baseline.json re-snapshotted. Nothing committed; pointer moves to next unblocked item.
items.note: Decision recorded: trailing-5 chosen over expanding to keep window width (5 laps) comparable to the block-bucket width it replaces. Expanding would pool early-race and late-race track states, which is the same pooling defect 02d identified and is fixing in int_sc_hazard_history - a decision to solve in that item, not to recreate here. Lap 2 goes NULL by design (no valid predecessor in the trailing-5 window); no back-fill attempted as that would reintroduce the leak precisely where the old model failed. The cost (2.22pp lap-grain coverage) is deterministic on lap_number (a contract axis via age_in_stint) and is non-leaking, so it is declarable rather than hazardous. AMENDED 2026-09-11 by 02c: three defects in the rebuild, all repaired under 02c, all recorded in the leaf doc. (1) GRAIN. The block bucket collapsed field_medians with a GROUP BY; the window functions that replaced it do not, and corners_with_keys is at driver grain, so the LEFT JOIN back onto (race_year, race_id, corner_name, lap_number) fanned the model out by the field size: 2,206,939 -> 38,444,069 rows (17.4x) against a corner_id that schema.yml declares unique. Duplicates carried identical values (verified: zero corner_ids with more than one distinct value), so no downstream MEAN or MEDIAN moved and nothing looked wrong - but the COUNTs did, and mart_corner_skill_driver's HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100 and PHASE_MIN_CELLS=30 gates were being cleared ~17x too easily while its LORO baseline silently became field-size weighted. Fixed with QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() = 1; the dedupe is value-preserving because the RANGE frame makes every driver row at one lap a peer with an identical frame. (2) field_corner_sample_n was floored to NULL below 5, contradicting its own not_null test in the same schema.yml block (416,639 failing rows) and destroying the companion column's only purpose. Now unfloored per the trailing_observation_count contract. (3) model_hashes.baseline.json was re-snapshotted against dev.duckdb rather than the ci.duckdb the oracle is defined over, which would have failed CI Gate 1c on all seven mandatory fct_* marts; regenerated from a full --target ci build. ROOT CAUSE: 02g ran one singular test and never ran dbt test / dbt build on the model, so the generic unique and not_null tests that name defects 1 and 2 directly never executed.
items.gates_run: No formal gates (rebuild only, no ablation). Definition of done RE-VERIFIED under 02c after repair: backward-only median in place; assert_corner_trailing_window_no_forward_reach rewritten to recompute the backward row supply by an explicit self-join inequality (not the window under test) and shown non-vacuous - 56,316 violating groups under the old block bucket, 0 now; corner_id unique restored; lap-2 rule declared in schema.yml; mart_corner_skill_driver rebuilt and its change reported; model_hashes.baseline.json re-snapshotted from a clean CI build (--check passes, 7/7 fct_* byte-stable).

A naive nine-column arm would likely have cleared on the coverage channel and been read as the driver-input mechanism - and the permutation-null arm does not catch it, because row-shuffling moves the NaNs with the values. items.title: Feasibility - does the first stage survive conditioning?
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-10 as DONE, verdict GO on 07b - not dissolved and not a dead end. Closed rather than left MEASURED on the user's ruling against D6: the item's definition of done (a matched-pair count with the conditioning set stated, plus a go/no-go) is fully met, and as a counting exercise it can never reach GATED - gates 2 and 3 have no meaning with no fit and gate 7 was declared not applicable in advance - so MEASURED would have blocked 07b permanently behind an item that had already answered its question. 08g is the precedent: a diagnostic item whose deliverable is a written finding closes on the finding. GO on 07b. The first stage survives conditioning and strengthens under it. Risk-set panel of 90,597 (stint, lap) moments over the 5,360 uncensored stints; Z = SC/VSC lap, pit = the stint's final lap. Unconditional pit hazard 0.2067 vs 0.0469 (RR 4.41). Conditioning ladder circuit -> era -> wet race -> tyre-age bin -> pre-SC degradation tercile: MH pooled RR 4.41 -> 4.41 -> 6.56 -> 7.42, RD +0.160 -> +0.304. All three pre-registered thresholds hold at the strictest rung L5a (retention 31.1% >= 30%, 2,059 pairs >= 500, RR 7.42 >= 2.0), so the rule returns GO not conditional-go. The one marginal number, 31.1% retention, decomposes into 31.4% covariate availability x 98.9% cell survival - missingness in deg_state_s (undefined for lap_in_stint <= 5 by construction), not the shattering the threshold was written to catch. Rules on threats 1 and 4 only: threat 2 (the SC bundles 'pitted earlier' with 'pitted cheaply') is untouched and is now the binding problem, and threat 3's exclusion restriction still needs arguing per outcome. Verified independently by the orchestrating session, which reproduced every rung to four decimals, closed the flag-provenance question in the verdict's favour (is_safety_car_lap is REGEXP_MATCHES(track_status,'.*4.*') in stg_laps.sql - race control, no pit input - and 96.89% of lap slices are field-unanimous), and found one bounded caveat the agent missed: boundary laps spanning a status change carry 30.2% of the treated pit moments and are mechanically inflated (pit laps flagged 85.6% vs 42.9% there). Stripping all of them leaves L5a RR 6.95 on 1,337 pairs, so GO holds; but it also means Ladder B's onset restriction is the LESS conservative choice, not the more. MEASURED not GATED: gates 2/3 substituted (no fit exists), 4 run in substance (200 within-cell permutations, null RR 0.9933 +/- 0.0711 vs observed 7.4225), 5 asserted, 6 run properly, 7 declared N/A in advance.

items.title: The IV estimator, with the exclusion restriction argued per outcome
items.note: UNBLOCKED 2026-09-10 by 07a's GO, and deliberately NOT started - the user's call on D6 was to close 07a and hold the 1-2 week spend. Runnable whenever wanted; nothing further is needed to begin. Design written only once the first stage is known to survive - 07a says it does (GO). Pre-register the arms before running them. Five things 07a hands it: (1) fold red flag into Z - 103 red-flag-only control moments are all stint ends, hazard 1.000; (2) race_to_track misses 2018_14; (3) conditioning on pre-SC degradation costs 47.9% of treated pit decisions non-randomly, so the estimand is a LATE over stints past their fifth lap unless a lap-2-capable degradation measure is built; (4) exact-cell matching will not do at L5a (19.2% of retained treated mass in cells with min < 5) - needs coarsened matching, a propensity score, or regression-adjusted stratification; (5) the boundary-lap channel the review found - either restrict Z to neutralisations already running at lap start, or carry the unanimous-slice cut as the headline robustness row. items.title: Competing-risks evaluation, with the dependent-censoring caveat stated
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-10; METRICS CORRECTED AND RE-RUN 2026-09-10. Evaluated the 10b-trained model (stint_life_regressor_v11) with cause-specific IPCW-Brier, time-dependent AUC and D-calibration on cv_final_fold (train 2018-2023, eval 2024, n=20,272 laps). HEADLINE (green_pit = tyre-limit, n=9,270 laps): IPCW-Brier 0.141, time-dependent AUC 0.844, calibration slope 1.23. The slope is the actionable finding - observed risk exceeds predicted in 4 of 5 bins and the gap widens with risk, so the model over-predicts stint life, worst for the stints it already flags as fragile. OVERALL ROW IS DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, DO NOT QUOTE (Brier 0.093, AUC 0.924): under the 10b variant green_pit is the only uncensored cause, so 'overall' scores green-pit events against an at-risk pool that is 54% non-green, and those causes differ in length by construction (race_end 26.4 laps mean vs green_pit 20.4 vs red 5.3). A model scores well there by separating cause membership, not by understanding tyre limits - the same mixture artefact 10c exists to remove. 0.844 is the defensible number. OTHER CAUSES: all 100% censored by definition under 10b, so no events to score and metrics are undefined (recorded as n/a, not as numbers). 10c therefore delivered ONE clean stratum, not per-cause comparison; cross-cause comparison needs a cause-specific hazard that 10b did not train. DEPENDENT CENSORING: stated qualitatively, band NOT quantified. The earlier 'dependence strength 1.2x' figure is WITHDRAWN - cause determines censoring status under 10b, so cause-specific censoring rates are 0/1 by construction and their spread measures the definition, not censoring/tyre-state dependence; it also fed a band of tau in [0, min(0.5, .)] which returns [0, 0.5] for any input. Quantifying it needs an instrument for SC arrival - see 07a. METRIC BUGS FOUND AND FIXED (all pre-existing in ml/src/survival.py, all before the numbers were used): (1) d_calibration was a tautology - it evaluated each row's survival curve at its own predicted median, so z == 0 and predicted risk was exactly 0.5 for every row; all 5 bins collapsed and the slope came back null. The observed side matched, using KM at each bin's own median. Both now use a shared horizon. This is why the superseded note's 'calibration slope ~1 (unbiased)' was unsupported - there was no slope, only one degenerate point; true slope 1.23. (2) ipcw_brier was not IPCW - both branches of its if/else were identical and weights ignored the horizon, scoring rows censored before t as though they had failed by t; now Graf et al. weighting. (3) time_dependent_auc counted ties as discordant and let y == t sit in both risk sets; ties now take half credit, at-risk is strictly y > t, and the O(n^2) loop is vectorised. Superseded figures: green-pit AUC 0.829, overall Brier 0.116, overall AUC 0.916. Full results in ml/artefacts/10c_evaluation_results.json and _improvements/reference/10c_evaluation_framework.md. ESTIMATOR VALIDATED: on data drawn from the lognormal AFT the metric assumes (calibration correct by construction) the repaired d_calibration returns slope 1.03 at 0% censoring, 0.98 at 20%, 0.93 at 40%. green_pit has no censoring within it, i.e. the 1.03 case, so the 1.23 is the model's miscalibration and not the metric's bias. Eight regression tests added in ml/tests/test_survival.py covering all three metrics (26 pass); they had no test coverage at all before, which is how the tautology survived a full measurement run.

items.title: GPBoost variance-components probe - measurement only, ships nothing
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-08. Ships nothing, as specified. Pre-registration + full results in work/05-model-family.md. HEADLINE: degradation_regressor_p50 sits AT its model-based noise floor to within +/-1.5% -- arm 2's Error_var 9.8103 implies a p50 pinball floor of 1.0024 against the achieved 1.0163386 (1.4% headroom), and the optimism-corrected 10.3865 implies 1.0314, i.e. above achieved. Evidence toward closing 05a, deliberately NOT acted on: this is one leg of a three-leg bracket and 01a/01b have not run. For 01b to close the bracket it must return an eval-population irreducible-noise estimate; this leg's value is sigma = 2.8335 s -> pinball 1.0024, and it is a LOWER bound. Gate 4 passed decisively (information 22.9325 vs capacity 0.5762, ~40:1). GATE 3 DID NOT DELIVER -- the GPBoost config has no bagging/feature_fraction so the fit is deterministic and the 5-reseed floor came back exactly 0.0000; arm 0c's sampling distribution is the substitute. Second finding: the between-stint variance in this target is almost entirely a 5-lap-window-overlap artifact (REML stint 5.3388 -> 0.0004, ceiling.py ANOVA ICC 0.1748 -> 0.0213 on non-overlapping rows). Third: driver and constructor carry no measurable variance in this target. Cannot go terminal until 01a/01b supply the other bracket legs. SESSION 2026-09-08 (late) — repair pass, three changes. (1) The IPW sensitivity arm had never run: the original arm2.py passed sample weights to gpb.Dataset(weight=), which gpboost 1.7.4 rejects (they belong on GPModel(weights=)), and it died there before its json.dump, losing arms 2/2b/3/3b to the log. Rerun with the weights NORMALISED to mean 1 — raw survival_weight averages 1.7126 and gpboost divides the nugget by weights[i], so raw weights would have rescaled Error_var against arm 2 for reasons unrelated to the reweighting. Result: race 1.1826 · stint 3.0516 · driver 0.0004 · constructor 0.0154 · Error_var 9.2769, TOTAL 13.5269 against arm 2's 13.5343. The total is invariant but the composition is not — reweighting moves ~0.53 out of Error_var into race and stint, so the floor leg is weight-sensitive: 0.9747 (4.1% headroom) against arm 2's 1.0024 (1.4%). Report both; the headline's +/-1.5% understates the modelling-choice spread. (2) 2024 eval sanity check, also never run: rmse 3.4726 and 0.5*MAE of the conditional MEAN 1.1428 on 13,896 rows against the achieved 1.0163386. The probe's mean fit is ~12% worse than production at alpha=0.5, as expected for a mean fit on a skewed target, but it confirms these components come from a WEAKER model than the one whose headroom they bound. (3) A thin-2 arm was run to try to rescue arm 3b. It does NOT: every 2nd lap is position-locked in exactly the way arm 3b already documents (always keeps stint position 0), so var(y) is 43.4841 against 40.1149 on all rows — the same population bias at half strength, plus the same unmeasured capacity-per-row optimism. stint survives at 1.2714 (it did not collapse) and Error_var is 12.8627, whose eval-population floor 1.1478 sits ABOVE the achieved 1.0163 and is therefore self-falsifying. Thinning is monotone across 1/2/5 — stint 2.7022/1.2714/0.0000, Error_var 9.8103/12.8627/17.3058, floor 1.0024/1.1478/1.3313 — which is consistent with arm 3c but adds nothing to it. ARM 3C REMAINS THE ANSWER TO THE OVERLAP QUESTION; no tree-fitted thinned arm is quotable at any thinning level. GATE 3 SUBSTITUTE, now COMPLETE: a cluster bootstrap over races (5 draws, races resampled with replacement, race and stint ids re-labelled per draw so a duplicated race acts as an independent draw rather than doubling one group; rounds fixed at 1,499) as a REAL gate-3 substitute — arm 0c measures estimator noise at a fixed synthetic truth, whereas this perturbs which races were actually observed, which is the gate-3 question. First draw alone moved Error_var 9.8103 -> 7.3782 and stint 2.7022 -> 4.3017, so the spread looks WIDE and may well disqualify quoting any headroom percentage. Script and running checklist: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-justin-github-off-the-pace/045b3d75-f4c9-4629-9680-c535ddef5e12/scratchpad/{arm5.py,arm5.json,arm5.log,CHECKLIST.md}. Nothing from this session is committed and nothing lands in the repo; the probe stays throwaway per foundations/epistemics.md. CAVEAT on the in-flight bootstrap: use its sd as the error bar, never its mean as a point estimate — draws 0 and 1 gave Error_var 7.3782 and 7.8434 against the full-data 9.8103, biased down because a draw holds only ~63% distinct races while rounds stay fixed at 1,499, raising capacity per distinct row above arm 2's. BOOTSTRAP RESULT (complete): Error_var draws 7.3782 / 7.8434 / 9.0440 / 7.2143 / 8.6362, sd 0.7938, which propagates to a floor sd of 0.0446 and a gate-style 2*sqrt(2)*sd of 0.1263. The 1.4% headroom is 0.0140 in absolute pinball — 0.31x that sd and 0.11x the 2*sqrt(2)*sd threshold — and the floor's +/-1.96sd interval 0.9149..1.0899 CONTAINS the achieved 1.0163386. The IPW variant's larger 4.1% headroom (0.0416) is still only 0.93x the sd, so the 1.4%-vs-4.1% modelling-choice spread is itself inside the noise and is not a real disagreement. GATE 3 THEREFORE FAILS on the programme's own convention. The headline must be restated: degradation_regressor_p50's achieved loss is INDISTINGUISHABLE from its model-based noise floor, and NO headroom percentage — not 1.4%, not +/-1.5% — is quotable from this probe. Direction only. 05c stays MEASURED.

This item must be sourced from real press.pirelli.com nomination posts or season-recap articles, cited per season, not regenerated from a model's prior knowledge -- see work/08-foundations-repair.md. items.title: Fix the stint-life calibration defect - the model over-predicts tyre life
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-10. THE DEFECT AS SPECIFIED DOES NOT EXIST AS DESCRIBED: the 1.232 slope was an IN-SAMPLE number, and out of sample the slope is 0.666 - on the other side of 1.0. GATE 1 CAUGHT IT, which is what gate 1 is for. evaluate_10c.py loaded the shipped stint_life_regressor_v11.bst and scored it on cv_final_fold's eval rows, but train.py refits the shipped booster on EVERY training season and training_seasons is 2018-2024, while the eval fold IS 2024 - so every 10c number measured memorisation. Reproduced to six decimals before anything was built on the repair: an all-seasons refit under the 10b label returns green-pit Brier 0.141216 / AUC 0.844167 / slope 1.231641 against 10c's published 0.1412159702194419 / 0.8441673881692147 / 1.2316409494909957, with the 5-bin table matching row for row. OPTIMISM on identical eval rows: AUC 0.8344 in-sample vs 0.6914 honest (+0.1429), Brier 0.1407 vs 0.2059 (-0.0652), slope 1.2346 vs 0.6664 (+0.5682). The slope does not merely shrink across that gap, it CROSSES 1.0, so 10c reported the miscalibration with the WRONG SIGN and every downstream statement inherits that. AUC 0.844 is NOT the incumbent; 0.691 is. Two further facts fell out: the .bst had been rewritten by a standard-variant retrain (training log stint_life_regressor_v11_20260910T092333.json) AFTER 10c ran, so 10c's description of the artefact as 'the 10b-trained model' was already false when it was read; and tune.py calls load_features with the default censoring_variant='standard' over 2018-2024, so max_depth 8 and scale 0.8 were selected against the OTHER label construction, on the mixture NLL 10c said not to use as a headline, with 2024 in the validation set. HONEST BASELINE (refit 2018-2023, scored 2024, 10b labels, tuned v11 params): green-pit slope 0.666, 95% [0.463, 0.906] on a 200-draw race-level cluster bootstrap over 24 eval races, 99.5% of draws below 1.0; AUC 0.691; Brier 0.206. Gate-3 reseed floor with XGBoost's seed genuinely varied (10b's zero-variance reseed table came from not varying it): slope sd 0.006208, floor 2*sqrt(2)*sd = 0.017559; AUC sd 0.001256, floor 0.003554. 10c's SELECTION CHECK SURVIVES, only its sign changed: out of sample zero-SC races 0.6555 (n=7,588, 16 races) vs SC races 0.7823 (n=1,682, 8 races) vs all races 0.6664 - both strata sit well below 1.0, so selection does not explain the defect. ARMS, all selected on the training side only (expanding season folds inside 2018-2023; nothing selected on the 2024 rows). A1 - THE AFT SCALE IS NOT THE LEVER, the clearest negative of the four: across 0.30-1.40, a 4.6x range, the inner-fold green-pit slope moves only 0.537->0.622 and never reaches 0.63; on 2024 the best scale buys +0.022 slope for -0.007 AUC (2.0x the AUC floor), paying more in discrimination than it returns. The inner-CV NLL optimum under the 10b label is 0.90 not the shipped 0.80, so the scale IS mis-set - it just does not matter here. A2 - THE DISTRIBUTION IS NOT THE LEVER EITHER and R2's skew statistic was measured on the wrong quantity: screened on XGBoost's own aft-nloglik over the inner folds, normal 1.8364 beats extreme 1.8650 and logistic 1.8876, so the arm selects the incumbent and nothing needs plumbing through laps_from_margin, the ONNX export and app/src/ml/survival.ts (extreme would have needed all three, its standardised median being log(log 2) = -0.3665, not 0). The reason the direction fails: skewness -0.829 and excess kurtosis 5.218 are properties of the TARGET IN LAPS, but AFT assumes the LOG-SCALE RESIDUAL is normal, and that residual is skew -0.443 / excess kurtosis -0.063 - already near-normal on the scale the model actually uses. A3 - the label construction is worth revisiting, but not for the slope: standard and 10b are indistinguishable on slope (0.700 vs 0.666, 1.9x floor, paired interval straddling zero), but standard is BETTER on green-pit Brier out of sample, 0.190 vs 0.206, better on the level bias (mean log residual -0.285 vs -0.434) and costs no AUC. 10b's label change makes green-pit WORSE out of sample on the metric 10c chose as its headline - a finding about 10b, recorded for whoever rules on it. A4 - CAPACITY IS THE LEVER, and the relationship is monotone. Inner-fold slope 0.794 / 0.708 / 0.680 / 0.669 / 0.656 / 0.622 at max_depth 2/3/4/5/6/8, while inner-fold NLL ALSO improves (1.8171 / 1.8090 / 1.8078 / 1.8130 / 1.8188 / 1.8364) - the shipped max_depth 8 is worse on the training folds' own headline metric, which is what you expect from hyperparameters selected under a different label construction. On 2024: depth 3 slope 0.879 (AUC 0.687, 1.2x AUC floor), depth 2 slope 1.074 (AUC 0.683, 2.5x), against A0 0.666 (AUC 0.691). Depth 2 and the standard-label cross are UNDECLARED extensions added after seeing the monotone trend, logged as such; the declared A4 winner is depth 3. Mechanism visible in the fit: the sd of the margin over green-pit eval rows falls 0.642 -> 0.509 -> 0.418 as depth goes 8 -> 3 -> 2. The incumbent's risk score was OVER-DISPERSED relative to its real skill, which is exactly what a slope below 1.0 means. THE TRADE-OFF THAT WAS NOT ANTICIPATED, and the reason this does not close as a win: reducing capacity fixes the DISPERSION of the risk score and leaves the LEVEL where it was. The calibration intercept only moves +0.271 -> +0.192 -> +0.180 across depth 8/3/2, the mean log-scale bias gets WORSE (-0.434 -> -0.524 -> -0.560), and observed risk still exceeds predicted in ALL FIVE bins at every depth. Restated in the brief's own terms: 'the model says 0.781 and the tyre is finished 0.946 of the time' honestly reads 'the model says 0.533 and the tyre is finished 0.749 of the time' - a ~22-point gap in the same dangerous direction, and NONE of the four declared arms closes it. That residual bias may not be a defect at all: under the 10b label the model estimates the LATENT TYRE LIMIT and green-pit endings are realisations that stopped at or before it, so a median above the observed ending is what the framing PREDICTS - which is also why A3's Brier is better, standard targeting the realised ending, which is what the gauge claims to show. That is the product question in D5, not a statistical one. GATE 7 - e-values as declared (Construction A, c=1.5, lambda=4/3, sd=0.006208, E=exp(0.8889*(z-1))): A1 3.78, A2 0.41, A3 12.4, A4 depth 3 9.3e8, A4x depth 2 1.1e11. THOSE LAST ARE NOT EVIDENCE AT THAT STRENGTH AND THE CONSTRUCTION IS WHAT IS WRONG, NOT THE ARITHMETIC: the pre-registered scale is the RESEED sd, which measures refit noise, while the uncertainty actually governing a slope estimated from 24 races is SAMPLING noise, which the cluster bootstrap puts at sd 0.10-0.19 - 16-30x larger. Feeding a scale 25x too small into exp() is how you get 1e11. Reported as declared per gate 7, then read correctly on the instrument that matches the estimand - the paired race-cluster bootstrap, both arms scored on the SAME resampled races so the shared race-draw noise cancels - where every delta straddles zero: A1 +0.0211 [-0.0101, +0.0549] P=0.870; A3 +0.0212 [-0.0721, +0.1334] P=0.630; A4 depth 3 +0.1726 [-0.1389, +0.3103] P=0.945; A4x depth 2 +0.1695 [-0.3081, +0.4029] P=0.855. gates.md already says the floor and the e-value are two instruments that must be allowed to disagree in public; here a third disagrees with both and it is the one to believe. GATE 4 - inapplicable in its literal form and STATED rather than skipped: no arm adds a column (A1/A2/A4 change how the same 32-feature matrix is fitted, A3 moves only the label bounds), so capacity is identical between every arm and A0 and the nuisance parameter the permutation null exists to remove is exactly zero BY CONSTRUCTION. The declared substitute, the 5-seed reseed null, was run and is the gate-3 floor above. DEFINITION OF DONE, ANSWERED. Does the slope move toward 1.0? Yes, materially: 0.666 -> 1.074 at depth 2 (declared winner depth 3: 0.879), a 78% reduction in |slope - 1|, and both bootstrap intervals now contain 1.0 where the incumbent's excluded it in 99.5% of draws. Without costing discrimination? Nearly - against the honest incumbent AUC of 0.691, depth 3 costs 0.0043 (1.2x the AUC reseed floor) and depth 2 costs 0.0088 (2.5x). Small, real, and priced. NOT LANDED, DELIBERATELY, and the verdict flags this as a judgment call for review -> D4. (1) The paired bootstrap cannot establish the improvement at 95% on 24 eval races, and overwriting the shipped booster on a 0.945-probability result is exactly the move 04a's multiplicity finding exists to discourage. (2) The right fix is not a hand-picked max_depth: the whole tuned parameter set was searched under the standard label, on the mixture NLL, with 2024 in the validation folds. Depth is the symptom the calibration slope happened to expose; the re-search is the actual repair -> 10e. (3) The level bias survives every arm, so shipping a slope fix would move a number the app shows without fixing what it shows. LANDED INSTEAD: THE INSTRUMENT. ml/src/evaluate_10c.py now refits on the training side by default (mode='honest', through evaluate.py's own _evaluation_split/_fit) and keeps the shipped-booster path only as an explicitly labelled in_sample diagnostic, printed beside the headline as an optimism gap so the failure cannot recur silently. The 26 ml/tests/test_survival.py regression tests are untouched and pass - the metrics were never the problem, the model being scored was. _improvements/reference/10c_evaluation_framework.md carries a correction block and every superseded figure is marked. STAGE IS MEASURED, NOT GATED: gate 4 was substituted rather than run and no model change shipped, and gates.md is explicit that an item which skips a step is MEASURED, never GATED.

items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-10. D5 settled first (realised stint ending / standard label; recorded on D5 below). WINNER S1x (censoring_variant=standard, max_depth 8, n_estimators 100, lr 0.0219, scale 0.754, interior on every axis - full params in the leaf doc): vs the standard-label incumbent A0 (slope 0.700/AUC 0.694/Brier 0.190), S1x reaches slope 0.903 (boot 95% [0.643,1.190]), AUC 0.715, Brier 0.167 - better on ALL THREE simultaneously, no trade, and it is the arm 10d's own framework did not predict (10d expected low depth; S1x kept depth 8 and cut shrinkage instead - n_estimators*learning_rate 5.26->2.19). Paired race-cluster bootstrap (the instrument 10d ruled authoritative over reseed floors and e-values): slope improvement +0.173 [-0.117,+0.273] P=0.930 - straddles zero, same ceiling as 10d's own +0.173 at P=0.945, 24 races still can't resolve a slope. Brier improvement +0.0237 [+0.0067,+0.0368], 200/200 draws improve - the one number here that IS significant at 95%, because a proper per-row score has far less sampling variance than a 5-bin slope. LEVEL BIAS: reproduced exactly as this doc warned for the slope-only arm S2 (mean log bias -0.2848->-0.3570, worse, mirroring 10d's -0.434->-0.560 under 10b) but S1x broke the pattern - Brier prices level as well as dispersion, and S1x's mean log bias moved -0.2848->+0.0681 (intercept +0.2234->+0.0068): the bias didn't close, it flipped sign and shrank 76%, now erring conservative (gauge slightly underestimates remaining life) instead of the incumbent's dangerous direction (overestimates it) - a product judgment, not just a statistical one, on top of D5. decisions.question: Land 10d's capacity fix (max_depth 8 -> 3, or 2) now, or wait for 10e's re-search?
decisions.context: 10d measured the fix and declined to land it, and its verdict explicitly flags that as 'a judgment call that should be reviewed'. FOR LANDING: the green-pit calibration slope moves 0.666 -> 0.879 (depth 3) or 1.074 (depth 2) against an incumbent whose bootstrap put 99.5% of draws below 1.0; that is a 78% cut in |slope - 1|, it clears the gate-3 reseed floor by 12-15x, and it costs only 0.0043 (depth 3) or 0.0088 (depth 2) of AUC against the honest incumbent 0.691. AGAINST: the paired race-cluster bootstrap - the instrument that matches the estimand - cannot establish it at 95% on 24 eval races (P(improves) 0.945 at depth 3), and 04a's multiplicity finding exists to discourage shipping on exactly that; a hand-picked max_depth is not the principled repair when the whole tuned set was searched wrongly (10e); and the LEVEL bias survives every arm, so landing this moves a number the app shows without fixing what it shows. Note the incumbent is not innocent either - it is mis-tuned by its own inner-fold NLL. Deciding to wait is a decision to keep shipping a booster whose risk score is known to be over-dispersed. UPDATED 2026-09-10 by 10e's re-search (see 10e's note): 10d's depth-2 fix is now STRICTLY DOMINATED by a different candidate, 10e's S1x (censoring_variant=standard per D5, max_depth 8, n_estimators 100, lr 0.0219, scale 0.754 - a shrinkage fix, not a depth fix). S1x also does NOT reproduce 10d's level-bias-survives-every-arm finding the way C2 does - its mean log bias flips sign and shrinks 76% rather than worsening. Note too: 10d's own C2 row was under-described (only 'depth 2', not the scale 0.90 needed to reproduce it) - re-verified by 10e. So this decision is no longer just 'ship 10d's depth fix or wait' - there are now two candidate parameter sets on the table (10d's C2, 10e's S1x) and S1x looks like the better one on every metric measured so far, though neither clears e-BH's multiplicity bar (10e: best E=35.9 vs threshold 80) or the paired-bootstrap slope test (both P~0.93, straddling zero) at 95%. Neither 10d nor 10e recommends landing on their own numbers; this decision is still open and now has more information, not less to weigh. REVIEWED AND HELD 2026-09-10, after 10e's verification pass: the user was walked through both candidates and chose to hold rather than land either. Reason: the Brier gain is real and significant, but e-BH rejects all four of 10e's declared arms and the slope gain straddles zero on the paired bootstrap, so landing would ship on evidence that does not clear the bar 04a exists to enforce - a promising lead, not an established fix. This is a HOLD, not a rejection: S1x's exact parameter set is recorded in 10e's note and in work/10-competing-risks.md so nothing has to be re-derived when the question is reopened. What would change the answer: a second eval season (2025 ingest) giving the slope test more than 24 races to work with, or a decision on the level-bias direction question that makes the conservative-erring gauge a positive rather than an open product call.

decisions.question: What should the app's stint-life gauge mean - the latent tyre limit, or the realised stint ending?
decisions.context: Raised by 10d section 6 and the closing section of work/10-competing-risks.md, and explicitly the user's call rather than a statistical one. Under the 10b label the model estimates the LATENT tyre limit; green-pit endings are realisations that stopped at or before it, so a predicted median above the observed ending is what the framing predicts, not a defect - which is why 10d's level bias (mean log residual -0.434, observed risk above predicted in all 5 bins) survives every arm and why A3's standard label scores better on green-pit Brier (0.190 vs 0.206). But the gauge reads that latent quantity to a user who interprets it as a realised stint - 'remaining stint life: 11 laps'. From the pit wall's point of view the realised answer, deployments included, is arguably the thing to predict. THE INCUMBENT ANSWERS NEITHER CLEANLY: it fits the marginal mixture - a tyre limit contaminated by a deployment process it cannot see coming, and a deployment process degraded by tyre variation. Splitting the causes lets the app choose, and lets it show both; int_sc_hazard_history (rebuilt by 02d) is the term that recombines them. SETTLE THIS BEFORE any recalibration of the level, and before 10e picks its censoring variant - it decides which label 10e should tune against.
decisions.resolution: Realised stint ending (the 'standard' censoring/label construction), not the latent tyre limit. The gauge reads as 'remaining stint life: N laps' and users interpret that as the realised answer, deployments included - matching the pit wall's own decision quantity. This is also the side the numbers already favour: 10d's A3 arm scores standard better than 10b on out-of-sample green-pit Brier (0.190 vs 0.206) with no AUC cost, and the 10b/latent framing carries a level bias that survives every capacity fix (mean log bias worsens -0.434 -> -0.560 as the slope improves), which is the wrong direction to be wrong in for a number read as safe laps remaining. 'Show both' was considered and set aside for now - it roughly doubles 10e's scope (two tuned models instead of one) plus app/UI work, and is worth revisiting later rather than blocking 10e. 10e tunes against the standard label.

decisions.question: 07a returned GO but is MEASURED, and board.py only counts GATED or terminal as satisfying a dependency - so 07b stays formally blocked. Start 07b anyway, close 07a, or leave it?
decisions.context: Not a doubt about the finding - 07a's verdict is GO and the reviewing session reproduced it independently. It is a bookkeeping gap with real cost behind it. 07a is a feasibility count that STRUCTURALLY CANNOT reach GATED: its own pre-registration declared gate 7 not applicable (it enters no hypothesis into the campaign family) and gates 2/3 have no meaning with no fit, so the stage rule that would unblock 07b can never be met by this item. Three ways out. (a) CLOSE 07a as terminal - its definition of done (a matched-pair count with the conditioning set stated, plus a go/no-go) is fully met, which is the 08g precedent for a diagnostic item whose deliverable is a written finding; this unblocks 07b mechanically. (b) Start 07b on an explicit override, leaving 07a MEASURED so the boundary-lap caveat stays visible. (c) Leave both as they are and spend the time elsewhere. What is actually being decided is whether to commit 1-2 weeks of fable-5.1 to the estimator now: 07b is the highest-value causal direction in the programme, and 07a says the instrument is there (RR 6.95-7.42 after full conditioning, 1,337-2,059 matched pairs). Against that, 07a discharged only threats 1 and 4 - threat 2, that the SC bundles 'pitted earlier' with 'pitted cheaply', is untouched, is the binding problem, and no amount of matched pairs helps with it. This is the same MEASURED-does-not-unblock gap the 2026-09-10 session flagged for 02b behind 10e, so whichever way it goes, it likely wants the same answer.
decisions.resolution: Option (a) with the spend held back: close 07a as terminal, leave 07b runnable but unstarted. 07a is CLOSED with its GO verdict intact and 07b moves BLOCKED -> SPEC. This rules on the bookkeeping, not on the research - 07b is wanted, just not now. The general question the gap raises (can a MEASURED item ever satisfy a dependency, which is also what sits under 02b behind 10e) was NOT decided here and is still open: this was settled case-by-case, by closing the item rather than by changing the rule.

decisions.question: Run 02c's arms on the degradation trio + cliff_classifier now and hold the stint_life_regressor column until 10e resolves, or wait and run all five targets together?
decisions.context: Raised by 02c's build session and recorded there as an ASSUMPTION rather than a ruling, which is why it is being promoted here: the next session reading 02c's history entry would otherwise take the four-target scope as settled. It is not. The bar on stint-life comes from 02b's note, which bars measuring that family's reseed floor until 10e resolves because 10d showed the shipped booster was tuned under the wrong label (D5 settled the label as the realised stint ending; 10e re-tunes against it). 02c inherited that bar BY ANALOGY - nobody has ruled that 02b's constraint generalises to other items. FOR RUNNING NOW (02c's own recommendation): the degradation trio is where Tier 2's entire rationale sits - per the leaf doc's section 1, corner inputs are the only lap-varying candidate and so the only one that can reach the target's 99.06% within-stint variance; a stint-life floor measured against a booster about to be retuned is measured against a moving target and would have to be re-run anyway; and holding the other four gains nothing. AGAINST: running the same arms twice against two different baselines adds a second selection event to the campaign family that 04a enumerated and 09b's e-BH operates over, so a channel that clears on the four-target pass and is then re-tested on stint-life has been tested twice - the multiplicity bookkeeping needs to say so in advance. NOTE this is the same shape as the general question D6 explicitly declined to settle - whether a MEASURED item can ever satisfy a dependency (02b behind 10e) - and it likely wants the same answer. Deciding either way is cheap; discovering the answer after 2-3 days of opus-5 is not.
decisions.recommendation: RUN NOW on the four targets - but fix the declared family BEFORE the run, naming the stint_life_regressor column as a deferred-execution arm rather than leaving it out. REASONING: multiplicity is the only argument against running now, and it is neutralisable rather than a real cost. e-BH (09b) operates over a PRE-REGISTERED family, so what creates a second selection event is ADDING the stint-life arm to the family after seeing the four-target results - not deferring the execution of an arm the family already named. Declare five, run four, and the split is bookkeeping. Against that, waiting buys nothing and costs real information: a stint-life reseed floor measured against the incumbent booster is measured against a model 10e is about to retune under the D5 label, so it would have to be re-run regardless - waiting does not save the work, it only delays the degradation answer that is 02c's entire rationale (leaf doc section 1: corner inputs are the only lap-varying candidate, so the only one that can reach the target's 99.06% within-stint variance). CAVEAT, and it is the bigger hazard: D3 is a larger threat to this ablation than D7 is. If 08e+08f land, the substrate under all five targets moves and 02c's arms need re-running whatever was decided here. Worth settling D3 before spending the run.
decisions.resolution: User's call, against the recommendation recorded above: wait and run all five targets together. 02c's arms A/B/C/P already ran on the degradation trio and cliff_classifier under the four-target scope 02c pre-registered before D7 was raised, and that run stands - it is not being redone. What this settles is how stint_life_regressor is handled: it is NOT folded into 02c's already-run family as a deferred-execution arm per the recommendation above. Instead it waits, and when 10e resolves the label the booster is tuned against, the stint-life arms run as their own pass rather than as an extension of this family's e-BH accounting. 02c's twelve declared hypotheses (A/B/C x four families) are the complete family for campaign-level e-BH purposes; the stint-life arms are a separate declaration when they run.
